//: Type checking, not building. Vite builds the JavaScript exactly as it did
before this file existed: `noEmit` is true and nothing here is on the
build's path.
Since the conversion of 2026-09-19 the **product source is TypeScript** —
every module of both packages' `src/`, and the machine's own tools — and it
is checked under `strict`. That is what this file is for now: a bare
argument in the code that makes the sound or draws the page is an error
rather than an omission nobody sees.
`strict` is on and `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is deliberately not. Turning
it on costs about nine hundred sites, nearly all of them an array indexed
inside a loop that has just measured its own length; a `!` on every one of
those is noise a reader has to see past rather than a fault anybody could
act on. It is written down here rather than left as an omission.
**What is not in `include`, and why.** The composer's tools
(`packages/deep-house/tools/`) and the repository's own (`tools/`) carry a
`.ts` extension and no types: they were renamed and not converted, because
the goal of the round was the product and not the tooling. Node runs them
the same either way — a `.ts` file with no annotations strips to itself —
and they stay out of the checker until somebody types them. The machine's
tools *are* in, because the two suites and the meters are what the record
is measured by and an untyped argument there is worth catching.
`allowJs` and `checkJs` stay on for the one JavaScript file left in the
source: `packages/engine/src/limiter-worklet.js`, which Vite copies out as
a raw asset rather than transforming, so TypeScript in it would reach an
AudioWorklet unparsed. It says so at the top of itself.
**Erasable syntax only**, everywhere. Node 24 runs `.ts` by stripping the
types and running what is left, which is what lets a tool run with no build
step — so no `enum`, no `namespace`, no parameter properties, `import type`
for a type, and `declare x: T` for a class field that is only a type.
`lib` carries DOM and DOM.Iterable because half of this is Web Audio and
the page; `types` names node because the machine's tools import node's own
modules, and `@types/node` came in with the conversion so they could.
**The one `.tsx` corner, and why it is one.** The machine view (step 1b of
2026-09-19, `packages/deep-house/src/machine/`) is React 19 by Eugene's own
decision — *"use React and decent tooling so the work is fast and
predictable"* — so `jsx` is `react-jsx` and `.tsx` joins `include`. It costs
nothing anywhere else: those files are bundled by Vite and are never run by
node, so the erasable-syntax rule above is untouched and there is still no
build step. The ring stays hand-drawn SVG in `.ts`, because pixel identity
and the `put()` discipline are its contract.
Since round W of PLAN-V1-NEXT the source is two packages and this is still
one program over both: `packages/engine` and `packages/deep-house` are
checked together, which is what makes the boundary a *type* error and not
just a lint — the app names the engine by its package name, npm's
workspaces link it, and `Bundler` resolution reads the engine's exports
map, so a name that is not on that map does not resolve here either. The
environment declarations are split the same way: the worklet's and the
worker's scope are the engine's, the page's surface and the build stamp
are the app's, and they merge because this is one program.
